codexIntegrationModes: MODE: codex app-server (PRIMARY integration surface, powers VS Code extension/desktop/web). INVOCATION: `codex app-server` (stdio, default), `codex app-server --listen ws://127.0.0.1:PORT` (WebSocket, experimental/unsupported), `--listen unix://[PATH]` (WebSocket-over-Unix-socket), `--listen off`; WS auth via --ws-auth capability-token/signed-bearer-token flags; health endpoints /readyz and /healthz in WS mode. TRANSPORT/WIRE: JSON-RPC 2.0 with the `jsonrpc` header omitted, newline-delimited JSON on stdio, one message per text frame on WS. HANDSHAKE: `initialize` (clientInfo + capabilities: experimentalApi, optOutNotificationMethods, requestAttestation) then `initialized` notification; experimental methods rejected without experimentalApi capability. PRIMITIVES: Thread > Turn > Item. KEY METHODS: thread/start, thread/resume, thread/fork, thread/read, thread/list, thread/archive, thread/delete, thread/name/set, thread/compact/start, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt, review/start, model/list, account/read, account/login/start, account/rateLimits/read, account/usage/read, skills/list, config/read, command/exec, fs/* (v2 filesystem API), `codex app-server generate-ts --out DIR` and `generate-json-schema --out DIR` emit version-pinned schemas. MATURITY: subcommand labeled Experimental in CLI reference but is the officially documented deep-integration path (developers.openai.com dedicated page; open source in codex-rs/app-server); stable-vs-experimental API split gated by capability flag; overload = JSON-RPC error -32001 'Server overloaded; retry later'. SOURCES: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md , https://openai.com/index/unlocking-the-codex-harness/

APP-SERVER EVENT/NOTIFICATION SCHEMA (what a chat UI actually receives — exact names). Thread: thread/started, thread/closed, thread/deleted, thread/status/changed (notLoaded|idle|active|systemError), thread/name/updated, thread/tokenUsage/updated (token counts). Turn: turn/started, turn/completed (final status incl. interrupted), turn/failed is exec-only — in app-server failures arrive via turn/completed status + error, turn/diff/updated (aggregated unified diff across all file changes — this is the ready-made 'diff view' feed), turn/plan/updated. Item lifecycle: item/started, item/completed. Streaming deltas: item/agentMessage/delta (assistant text chunks), item/plan/delta, item/reasoning/textDelta, item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta, item/reasoning/summaryPartAdded, item/commandExecution/outputDelta (stdout/stderr chunks). ITEM TYPES (card taxonomy): userMessage, agentMessage, plan, reasoning, commandExecution (command, status, output, exit code), fileChange (path, kind, diff), mcpToolCall, dynamicToolCall (experimental client-executed tools), collabToolCall, webSearch, imageView, enteredReviewMode, exitedReviewMode, contextCompaction. SERVER->CLIENT REQUESTS (approvals; UI must respond): item/commandExecution/requestApproval and item/fileChange/requestApproval (decisions: accept | acceptForSession | decline | cancel | acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment), item/permissions/requestApproval (permissions + scope session|turn), tool/requestUserInput (1-3 questions), mcpServer/elicitation/request; serverRequest/resolved clears pending prompts. Rate limits/usage: account/rateLimits/updated, account/updated. Misc: model/rerouted, model/safetyBuffering/updated, configWarning, warning. Error payloads carry codexErrorInfo (ContextWindowExceeded, UsageLimitExceeded, HttpConnectionFailed, ResponseStreamDisconnected, SandboxError, ...). SOURCE: https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server (full method+event reference)

MODE: codex exec --json (headless one-shot / CI). INVOCATION: `codex exec --json "prompt"`; resume with `codex exec resume --last` or `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>`; other flags: --output-schema <json-schema file> (validated structured final output), -o/--output-last-message <file>, --ephemeral, --sandbox workspace-write|danger-full-access, --ignore-user-config, --skip-git-repo-check. TRANSPORT: JSONL on stdout (note dot-separated names here vs slash-separated in app-server). EVENTS (exact): thread.started, turn.started, turn.completed, turn.failed, item.started, item.completed, error. Items cover agent messages, reasoning, command executions, file changes, MCP tool calls, web searches, plan updates — but NO token-level deltas and NO interactive approval round-trips (approvals are pre-resolved by sandbox/approval policy flags), so it cannot drive a live interactive chat UI, only batch/automation. MATURITY: Stable (alias `codex e`). SOURCES: https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive , https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference

MODE: codex mcp-server (Codex exposed AS an MCP server). INVOCATION: `codex mcp-server` over stdio. TRANSPORT: JSON-RPC over MCP transport; exposes the same v2 thread/turn method family (thread/start, thread/resume, turn/start, turn/steer, turn/interrupt, model/list, config/read, account ops) plus legacy v1 compat; emits typed v2 notifications (thread/started, turn/completed, ...) and codex/event/* stream notifications for live agent events; approval requests surfaced via MCP elicitation to the consuming client. Implemented on top of app-server-protocol types. MATURITY: subcommand listed Stable in CLI reference but the interface doc says 'experimental and subject to change without notice'; intended for agent-to-agent consumption (another agent using Codex as a tool), not for building a rich chat UI. Distinct from `codex mcp` which only manages MCP server config (list/add/remove/login). SOURCES: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/docs/codex_mcp_interface.md , https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference

MODE: codex proto — EFFECTIVELY GONE as a public surface (as of July 2026). The legacy low-level submission-queue/event-queue stdio stream (`codex proto`, protocol_v1) is absent from the current official CLI reference (which lists exec, app-server, mcp-server, mcp, sandbox, apply, resume, fork, review, remote-control, debug app-server send-message-v2, execpolicy); the app-server README and docs never mention it, and OpenAI's 'Unlocking the Codex harness' positions app-server as the extracted, documented protocol for all surfaces. The `protocol` and `app-server-protocol` crates still exist in codex-rs but as internal event-bus/type crates consumed by app-server/exec/tui, not a supported CLI mode. Do NOT build on `codex proto`; target app-server. SOURCES: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference , https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main/codex-rs , https://openai.com/index/unlocking-the-codex-harness/

SUPPORTING FACTS: schema generation (`codex app-server generate-ts` / `generate-json-schema`) outputs are version-specific — pin generated types to the installed Codex CLI version and regenerate on upgrade; WebSocket transport explicitly 'experimental and unsupported', stdio is the supported default; `codex debug app-server send-message-v2` exists for protocol testing; InfoQ coverage (Feb 2026) confirms app-server is the protocol unifying CLI/VS Code/web/desktop surfaces. SOURCES: https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/02/opanai-codex-app-server/ , https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog
opencodeUiAnatomy: ARCHITECTURE: strict client/server split. Running `opencode` starts (1) a background server (Hono-based HTTP, owns sessions/state/tools/providers, persists as daemon) and (2) a TUI client that talks to it over HTTP+SSE. `opencode serve --port 4096 --hostname 127.0.0.1 [--cors origin] [--mdns]` exposes the same backend to any client (desktop app beta, IDE extensions, CI); optional HTTP basic auth via OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD/OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME; OpenAPI 3.1 spec served at /doc; typed SDK generated from it (event.subscribe(), session.prompt(), session.command()). Sources: https://opencode.ai/docs/server/ , https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode

HTTP API SURFACE: /global/health; /global/event and /event = SSE stream (first event `server.connected`, then bus events like message/session/permission updates — this is how every client renders live streaming); /session CRUD + fork/share/summarize; /session/:id/message (send/list messages), /session/:id/command (run slash commands), /session/:id/shell (shell exec); /find (text search), /find/file (fuzzy file search), /file/content, /file/status; /config, /config/providers, /provider; /agent (list agents); /tui/append-prompt, /tui/submit-prompt, /tui/execute-command, /tui/control/next|response (remote-control the TUI itself). Messages are composed of typed Parts (e.g. { type: 'text', ... }; tool/reasoning/patch parts) — the part-array model is what lets tool calls and diffs render as discrete cards. Source: https://opencode.ai/docs/server/ , https://opencode.ai/docs/sdk/

TUI STACK: current TUI is written in SolidJS with the @opentui/solid terminal renderer (layout, scrolling, mouse support). Three-tier state: SyncProvider (server-synchronized state fed by the SSE event bus), LocalProvider (ephemeral client state), ThemeProvider. UI updates are event-driven: server pushes bus events, SyncProvider patches the reactive store, components re-render — the exact pattern a GUI should copy. Source: https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.2-terminal-user-interface-(tui) , https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.3-tui-application-bootstrap

MESSAGE LIST: scrollable conversation view with markdown rendering; Session route component (packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/routes/session/index.tsx) owns message history plus UI toggles for sidebar visibility, thinking/reasoning concealment, and timestamp display. Tool executions appear inline in the flow as collapsible detail blocks (`/details` toggles tool-execution detail visibility). Diffs render per `diff_style` config: 'auto' (adapts to terminal width, side-by-side when wide) or 'stacked' (single column). Sources: https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/ , https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.2-terminal-user-interface-(tui)

BOTTOM INPUT EDITOR: Prompt component (component/prompt/index.tsx) — multiline composition; `!` prefix runs bash; `/` prefix runs slash commands; `@` references files (auto-included as context) and agents; usePromptHistory (navigate previous prompts) and usePromptStash (draft stashing); auto-detects active files from your editor; `/editor` opens $EDITOR for long prompts. Autocomplete component (component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx) suggests files/agents/commands and inserts 'extmarks' — visual pills backed by structured data parts (not plain text). Source: https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.2-terminal-user-interface-(tui) , https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/

INTERACTIVE DIALOGS (approval UX): PermissionPrompt renders tool-execution requests WITH an inline diff view for file edits (approve/deny); QuestionPrompt renders agent questions with single/multiple choice and free-text input. This maps 1:1 onto Codex app-server's item/commandExecution/requestApproval + item/fileChange/requestApproval + tool/requestUserInput. Source: https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.2-terminal-user-interface-(tui)

SLASH COMMANDS + SELECTORS: /connect, /compact, /details, /editor, /exit, /export, /help, /init, /models, /new, /redo, /sessions, /share, /themes, /thinking, /undo, /unshare. Model selector via /models dialog; ctrl+t cycles model thinking variants; /sessions is the session switcher (session list presented as a dialog/sidebar rather than a permanent pane, sidebar visibility is a toggle). Keybindings use a leader key (default ctrl+x) with chords (ctrl+x c = compact, ctrl+x m = models), customizable. Undo/redo of agent changes are first-class commands. Source: https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/

CHROME/POLISH: theme system via /themes persisted in tui.json; mouse support on by default with scroll acceleration; desktop attention notifications when the agent asks a question or finishes; plugin slot system injects custom components into named UI slots (home_logo, home_footer); /share publishes a session to a web URL; /export dumps the transcript. Source: https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/ , https://deepwiki.com/sst/opencode/6.2-terminal-user-interface-(tui)
recommendations: Build the chat backend on `codex app-server` over stdio (JSONL JSON-RPC, header omitted): spawn one app-server per workspace, do initialize/initialized with your clientInfo, stay on the stable API (omit experimentalApi) and run `codex app-server generate-ts --out` at build time against the pinned Codex version to get exact TypeScript types for every method/event. Do not target `codex proto` (no longer a documented CLI surface) and do not use `codex exec --json` for the interactive UI (no deltas, no approval round-trips — keep it only for fire-and-forget automation).

Drive the message list off the item lifecycle, exactly like the official clients: create a card on item/started keyed by item id, stream into it (item/agentMessage/delta -> markdown text, item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta -> collapsible 'thinking' block, item/commandExecution/outputDelta -> terminal-style output pane), finalize on item/completed (exit code, final diff, tool result). Map item types to distinct card renderers: agentMessage, reasoning, commandExecution, fileChange (per-file diff), mcpToolCall, webSearch, plan, contextCompaction. Use turn/diff/updated for a turn-level aggregated 'Changes' diff panel and turn/plan/updated for a plan widget — Codex hands you both pre-computed.

Implement the three approval server-requests as blocking modal/inline cards that reply on the same JSON-RPC id: item/commandExecution/requestApproval and item/fileChange/requestApproval (buttons: accept, acceptForSession, decline, cancel) and item/permissions/requestApproval; plus tool/requestUserInput for agent questions. Show token/context state from thread/tokenUsage/updated and a rate-limit footer from account/rateLimits/updated. Handle turn/interrupt (stop button), turn/steer (send-while-running), and JSON-RPC error -32001 with backoff.

Imitate CodexMonitor (github.com/Dimillian/CodexMonitor, MIT, Tauri v2 Rust+React — the closest architectural cousin to this repo's Tauri app): one app-server process per workspace, thread resume on reopen, unread/running badges per thread, pin/rename/archive threads, per-thread drafts, Queue-vs-Steer toggle for follow-ups while a turn runs, image attachments in the composer, optional remote daemon mode. Also study codex-web (github.com/0xcaff/codex-web) for the thin-bridge pattern (proxy an already-running app-server over a unix socket) and codex-gateway/codex-tg for remote-control patterns.

Copy OpenCode's composer anatomy for the input UX: multiline bottom editor with @-file and /-command autocomplete rendered as structured pills (extmarks), ! prefix for raw shell, prompt history + draft stash, external $EDITOR escape hatch; a /details-style toggle for tool-call verbosity; diff_style auto/stacked toggle for narrow layouts; session switcher dialog + leader-key chords; desktop notifications on question/completion; and OpenCode's event-driven state pattern (single SSE/JSON-RPC event bus -> reactive store -> UI) which translates directly to app-server notifications feeding a frontend store over a Tauri event channel.

Version-resilience: the app-server schema is version-specific, so feature-detect at runtime (initialize response, model/list, experimentalFeature/list), tolerate unknown notification methods (ignore, don't crash), and use capabilities.optOutNotificationMethods to silence streams you don't render (e.g. raw reasoning deltas) to cut IPC volume.
